judgements.referenceQuote: Prior to being named CEO, Barra was executive vice president of global product development, purchasing, and supply chain
judgements.evidenceQuote: Prior to CEO, she was executive vice president of global product development, purchasing, and supply chain.

judgements.referenceQuote: Barra started working for General Motors in 1980 as a co-op student when she was 18 years old
judgements.evidenceQuote: She started working for General Motors in 1980 as a co-op student.
judgements.rationale: The dossier recovers the 1980 start as a co-op student (other claims add the General Motors Institute/Pontiac Motor Division detail), but it does not state that she was 18 years old, checked fender panels, inspected hoods, or worked to pay her college tuition, so only part of the reference fact is stated.

judgements.referenceQuote: Barra graduated from the General Motors Institute (now Kettering University) in 1985, where she obtained a Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering
judgements.evidenceQuote: She graduated with a bachelor of science degree in electrical engineering in 1985, followed by a master of business administration from the Stanford Graduate School of Business in 1990.
judgements.rationale: The dossier recovers the 1985 BSc in electrical engineering and the 1990 Stanford MBA, but it does not attribute the bachelor's degree to the General Motors Institute (now Kettering University) nor mention that the MBA was taken on a GM fellowship, so parts of the reference fact are missing.

judgements.referenceQuote: Barra was inducted into the engineering honor society Tau Beta Pi[10] (MI Zeta class of 1985) and the honor society IEEE-Eta Kappa Nu (Theta Epsilon chapter 1983) while at Kettering University
judgements.rationale: No dossier claim mentions induction into Tau Beta Pi or IEEE-Eta Kappa Nu at Kettering University, so the fact is not addressed at all.

judgements.referenceQuote: Today's GM will do the right thing. That begins with my sincere apologies to everyone who has been affected by this recall, especially the families and friends of those who lost their lives or were injured.
judgements.evidenceQuote: Mary Barra apologized publicly and profusely regarding the ignition-switch recalls.

judgements.referenceQuote: Sitting here today, I cannot tell you why it took so long for a safety defect to be announced for this program, but I can tell you we will find out.
